summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 12, part 60) set during a tense, dull evening in a household where Dr. Quelton and Captain Grey play chess while Mrs. Quelton lies on a chaise longue. Lexy, a restless young woman, sits reading without really attending, burdened by guilt over a secret act: she secretly replaced the contents of a tonic bottle with plain water, intending to stop a drug that has been harming Mrs. Quelton. She dreads that the doctor will discover the substitution and watches both Mrs. Quelton and the doctor with growing anxiety.
one_line: Lexy, anxious after secretly swapping Dr. Quelton's tonic for water, endures a tense evening watching the household and dreading discovery.
key_facts: Dr. Quelton and Captain Grey are playing chess at a small table in a haze of tobacco smoke.
Mrs. Quelton lies on her chaise longue, doing nothing at all.
Lexy finds the evening the most wearisome and depressing she has ever spent.
Lexy feels a sense of guilt lying like lead upon her heart.
Lexy fears the doctor will find out the substitution, expecting a day or two at the very most before discovery.
Lexy wonders whether there is already a faint and indefinable change in Mrs. Quelton's face.
Dr. Quelton once tapped the bottle and told Captain Grey that the preparation in it would make his fortune, if he chose.
Just before dinner Lexy ran up to the cupola, emptied the bottle into the sink, and refilled it from the tap.
Lexy chose the swap because the liquid in the bottle was colorless and almost without odor.
Lexy believed it was a plain and obvious duty to destroy the drug that so horribly affected Mrs. Quelton.
Lexy had found an undisturbed half hour when the doctor and Captain Grey were out.
Lexy had meant to wait and watch, and act when the moment came, hoping Mrs. Quelton would have a chance to return to a normal condition.
The text includes a stray sentence about the Semper Opera House being next to where Diana lives, which appears unrelated to the surrounding narrative.
